title: Pop a possibly empty bridge stack
statement: Let $c$ be a compiled program, let $x$ be a bridge input word, and choose optional bridge states $q,q'$, a valid input-head position $p$, an assignment $st$ of stacks to the four stack names, and an output word. For any stack name $k$, applying the action that blanks the current cell of the work tape for $k$ and moves its head one cell to the right if the stack at $k$ is nonempty, and otherwise leaves that head in place, with successor state $q'$, gives the bridge configuration with state $q'$ and the stack at $k$ replaced by its tail; all other stacks, the input-head position, and the output are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: An assignment $st$ of stacks to the four stack names
replaced:
The one-tape action on the tape of a stack name $k$ that blanks the current cell and
moves the head right precisely when the stack at $k$ is nonempty transforms a bridge
configuration into the bridge configuration whose stack at $k$ is replaced by its
tail (an empty stack remaining empty), with the input position and output unchanged.
